import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Numerator of $1/\det(M)$ for $M[i,j] = 1/\operatorname{lcm}(i,j)$

Numerator of $1/\det(M)$ where $M$ is the $n \times n$ matrix with
$M[i,j] = 1/\operatorname{lcm}(i,j)$.

*References:*
- [A060841](https://oeis.org/A060841)-/

namespace OeisA60841

/-- The $n \times n$ matrix with entry $(i,j)$ equal to
$1/\operatorname{lcm}(i+1, j+1)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. -/
def lcmMatrix (n : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℚ :=
  Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n ↦ 1 / ((Nat.lcm (i.val + 1) (j.val + 1) : ℚ))

/-- Numerator of $1/\det(M)$ where $M$ is the $n \times n$ matrix with
$M[i,j] = 1/\operatorname{lcm}(i+1,j+1)$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  ((lcmMatrix n).det)⁻¹.num

@[category test, AMS 11 15]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by
  decide +native

@[category test, AMS 11 15]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 4 := by
  decide +native

@[category test, AMS 11 15]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 18 := by
  decide +native

@[category test, AMS 11 15]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 144 := by
  decide +native

@[category test, AMS 11 15]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 900 := by
  decide +native

/-- The exceptional values of $n$ where $1/\det(M)$ is conjectured to be an integer. -/
def integerDetN : Set ℕ :=
  Set.Icc 1 34 ∪ {36, 38}

/--
"Conjecture: $1/\det(M)$ is an integer only for n: 1 to 34, 36 and 38.
All denominators are powers of two (A000079). - _Robert G. Wilson v_, Aug 02 2015"-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 15]
theorem conjecture :
    (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → (((lcmMatrix n).det)⁻¹.den = 1 ↔ n ∈ integerDetN)) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ k : ℕ, ((lcmMatrix n).det)⁻¹.den = 2 ^ k) := by
  sorry

end OeisA60841

status_issues.source_status: Disproved: Adamczewski's August 2026 paper gives n = 1807 as a counterexample to the power-of-two-denominator conjunct. The integrality classification is not refuted by this counterexample.
status_issues.evidence: OEIS A060841 now states: “Adamczewski disproves the above conjecture with counterexample for n = 1807, in linked article” (Michael De Vlieger, August 20, 2026). Appendix A.1 of arXiv:2608.11941v2 specifies that Σ_{k=1}^{1807}(2v₃(k) − v₃(φ(k))) = −1. Using 1/det(M_n) = (n!)²/∏_{k=1}^n φ(k), its reduced denominator is therefore divisible by 3 and cannot be a power of 2.
status_issues.suggested_change: Mark the combined conjecture research solved and document its negative resolution with the paper reference; when recording the resolved theorem, state the negation in accordance with repository conventions. Alternatively split the two conjuncts, recording the denominator claim as disproved without implying that the exceptional-size classification was disproved.

reformulations.difference: The source's integrality condition is expressed as the reduced rational denominator being 1, rather than as equality to an integer.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every r : ℚ, r.den = 1 iff ∃ z : ℤ, r = (z : ℚ). In the forward direction take z = r.num; conversely, every integer cast has denominator 1. Together with one_div, this identifies the Lean condition with the source's condition on 1/det(M). The equivalence of the complete conjunction with this integer-cast formulation was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the conjecture.

review.notes:
All nine declarations were checked. The Fin n indexing shifted by 1 correctly gives indices 1 through n. The five test values agree with OEIS and were independently checked in Lean. The extension at n = 0 has determinant 1 and is excluded from both conjectural assertions. There is no reachable zero-determinant default: the divisor-incidence factorization gives det(M_n) = ∏_{k=1}^n φ(k)/(n!)² > 0 for positive n.

Exact rational elimination checked the boundary sizes 33–41; a separate totient-product computation matched all 400 published numerators. The final scratch file compiles and also verifies the published finite valuation sum −1 using native_decide; this is an arithmetic check, not a formal proof of the determinant product formula. The main OEIS page was access-challenged, so its full entry was read through the official mirror. No repository files were edited.
